purpose: Meloxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It can also help with pain from other inflammatory conditions. It is not a pain reliever for general everyday aches like a headache — it works best for ongoing joint and inflammation-related pain.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Meloxicam blocks an enzyme called COX-2 that your body uses to make those chemicals. By reducing those chemicals, it helps decrease inflammation and pain in your joints and tissues.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or belly pain are the most common side effects. Some people get diarrhea, gas, or feel dizzy. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset. Headaches are also possible.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of heart attack or stroke, especially if taken for a long time or at high doses. It can also cause serious stomach bleeding or ulcers — watch for black or tarry stools or stomach pain. Do NOT take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Avoid it in the last 3 months of pregnancy. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney problems, high blood pressure, or a history of stomach ulcers. Do not take it with other NSAIDs like ibuprofen or naproxen.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual starting dose is 7.5 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may increase it to 15 mg once daily if needed. Always take the lowest dose that works for you, and try not to take it longer than necessary. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
